sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Advaita Vedanta**: The philosophy of **Non-dualism**, asserting that the individual soul (Atman) and the ultimate reality (Brahman) are identical.
• **Maya**: The concept of **Illusion**; the world is not non-existent but is a superimposition on Brahman, appearing real due to ignorance (Avidya).
• **Jnana Marga**: The path of **Knowledge** as the primary means to achieve Moksha (liberation), emphasizing intellectual inquiry over ritualism.
• **Institutional Legacy**: Established the **Dashnami Sampradaya** and four major **Mathas** (monasteries) to institutionalize Vedic learning across India.

items.definition: The three foundational texts of Vedanta: Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, and Brahma Sutras. Shankaracharya wrote commentaries on all three.
The ultimate reality without attributes or form, which is the focus of Shankaracharya's Advaita philosophy.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Shanmata**: The integration of six major deities (Ganesha, Surya, Vishnu, Shiva, Shakti, Skanda) into a unified worship system.
• **Debate Culture**: Used 'Shastrartha' (formal debate) to defeat Buddhist scholars, effectively shifting the intellectual center of gravity back to Vedic thought.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Accusations of being a 'crypto-Buddhist' (Prachanna Bauddha) due to the similarity between Advaita and Madhyamaka Buddhism.
• **Solutions**: Emphasizing the distinction between the 'Anatta' (no-self) of Buddhism and the 'Atman' (eternal self) of Advaita.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-D-P-B' (Sringeri, Dwarka, Puri, Badrinath).
• **Decoded Meaning**: South (Sringeri), West (Dwarka), East (Puri), North (Badrinath). Remember: 'S-D-P-B' follows a clockwise rotation starting from the South.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Shankaracharya is often confused with the Bhakti saints of the 12th-15th century (like Ramanuja or Kabir). Shankaracharya predates the Saguna Bhakti movement and focused on Jnana (Knowledge), not emotional devotion.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Cultural Unifier' to describe his role in creating a pan-Indian identity through the establishment of the four Mathas.

keyTakeaways: Shankaracharya was the primary architect of Advaita Vedanta (Non-dualism).
He established four cardinal Mathas to ensure the continuity of Vedic tradition.
His philosophy emphasizes Jnana (Knowledge) over ritualistic Bhakti.
